chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Kathīr, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

A man's eye was injured while it was still standing in place. So ʿAlī عليه السلام ordered that his sound eye be tied, and a man was stationed beside him with an egg in his hand, saying: “Do you see it?” When he said, “Yes,” he moved back a little, until when it became hidden from him, that place was marked.

He said: Then his injured eye was bandaged. He said: Then the man kept moving farther away while looking with his sound eye at the egg, until when it became hidden from him. Then the distance between the two was measured, and compensation was given according to that.

key_terms.أُصِيبَتْ: was injured; indicates bodily harm that became the subject of legal assessment
key_terms.الْأَرْشَ: financial compensation for injury; the assessed indemnity based on the extent of harm
key_terms.بَيْضَةٌ: an egg; the visible object used in testing the limit of sight
key_terms.خَفِيَتْ: became hidden; refers to the point at which the object could no longer be seen
key_terms.عَيْنُهُ الصَّحِيحَةُ: his sound eye; the unimpaired eye used as a point of comparison
key_terms.عَيْنُهُ الْمُصَابَةُ: his injured eye; the damaged eye whose visual impairment was being evaluated
key_terms.قِيسَ: was measured; indicates the measurement used to quantify the injury

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام assess compensation for partial loss of eyesight in an injured eye?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a judicial method attributed to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام for assessing damage to eyesight when the eye remains physically present but its vision is impaired. The ruling establishes a practical measurement to determine the extent of injury and calculate the appropriate financial compensation.
